The tit for tat system is more properly described as Quid Pro Quo and it is not open at all anymore Abramoff caused it to go underground. Sure a congressmen still knows which lobbyist will give you a check after you vote but more often than not money is given to get access rather than a vote. 10,000 a cycle can get you a phone call or a meeting when you need it; bundling 100,000 can get you just about anything you want congressionally although there are only three or four people who do that regularly. It should also be noted that bribery which is a specific amount for a specific action is still illegal as is campaigning on government property, in government buildings, or using government communications equipment. If you are talking about inter-government transfers of personnel then yes that is discussed openly although that is not anything out of the ordinary. What you might be thinking of are personnel transfers between Independence and K St. which are discussed in private between the aide and the hiring manager from the firm.
